headline: USTR Proposes Section 301 Tariffs for Fourteen Economies
deck: Written comments and hearing requests are due 5 January, with hearings set to begin 25 January.
body: United States Trade Representative Jamieson Greer determined that manufacturing policies in 14 economies are actionable under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974. [E1] The determinations cover China, the European Union, Singapore, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Japan and India; USTR made no determination on Mexico or Norway. [E2]

USTR proposed responsive actions, including additional tariffs subject to public comment and exemptions for certain products identified in annexes. [E3] Interested people must submit written comments and hearing requests by 5 January 2027; hearings on the proposed actions are scheduled to begin 25 January. [E4]

On 24 October, the paper forecast a 35% chance that an official U.S. record would name eligible Canadian-linked agricultural products and their effective date by 31 October. [E6] What has changed is that USTR has now made Section 301 determinations and put the proposed tariffs into a public-comment process. [E1][E3]
AP reported that an administration official said the tariffs remained at the proposal stage and gave no strict timetable for implementation. [E5]

evidence_box.fragment: Today, United States Trade Representative Jamieson Greer determined under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 that the acts, policies, and practices of 14 economies relating to structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors are unreasonable and burden or restrict U.S. commerce, and are thus actionable under Section 301(b) of the Trade Act.
